meaning_en: You are the witness of all and the support of the world. You pervade the moving and the unmoving; you are the doer who makes all do, the Lord of all. Everything that exists is you alone.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: The world, the people, and Janardan — you alone are the one complete whole. With qualities and without qualities, you alone, O mother and father.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Such is your fathomless greatness, which the Nigama and Agama scriptures themselves do not grasp. What then can be said, Purushottam, about this Ganu's lowly state?
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: When Ram's grace fell, then even the monkeys gained power, and the gops too became strong, on the banks of the Yamuna, in Gokul.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Let your grace take place; there is no need of wealth. When one is wholly devoted at your feet, you give help in that.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Now (I invoke) the primordial mother Saraswati, who is Brahma's prakriti (consort), the deity meditated upon by great poets — Brahmakumari Sharada.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: To that Jagadamba, let my prostrate (sashtang) salutation be. I am an ignorant child; may you bear with my pride (audacity).
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Your grace is so immense that even a cripple climbs a mountain, and a mute delivers an unbroken discourse in an assembly.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: May no shortcoming come to that glory of yours; please help Dasganu, who is composing this granth.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Now, O Puranapurusha, O Pandurang, lord of Pandhari, O Sachchidananda, Ramesha — 'Pahi mam' (protect me), O Dinabandhu (friend of the humble).
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Victory, victory to you of generous fame; victory, victory to you, light of splendor. Victory, victory to you, O Ganapati! O son of Gauri, O Mayureshwara!
At the start of any task, people remember you — great scholars, sages, saints, and virtuous men.
The deep power of your grace turns all obstacles to ashes — like a cotton wick before fire, O cloud of mercy!
check_note: The phrase 'कापुसाचा पाड' means 'a heap of cotton', not 'a cotton wick'. The simile compares obstacles to a heap of cotton before fire, not a wick. Corrected meaning: 'The unfathomable power of your grace turns all obstacles to ashes — like a heap of cotton before fire, O cloud of mercy!'

meaning_en: Therefore, with reverence I bow at your feet; may a sweet, lotus-like composition be made through Dasganu's mouth.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: I am ignorant and dull-witted, with no skill in poetry. But if you dwell in my mind, this task of mine will succeed.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: The pen draws out the letters, but the strength is not in the pen itself. It merely acts as the instrumental cause for the work in the form of writing.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Dasganu is the pen here; all you saints, please hold it. That the book be composed full of rasa — this itself is the prayer.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Now, listeners, be attentive; listen to the tale of the saint with a concentrated mind, so that your own welfare may come about.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Saints themselves, on this earth, are the walking, talking Parameshwar. They are oceans of vairagya (detachment) and bestow the state of moksha.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Saints are the true, manifest embodiment of the divine presence (sannidhi). Saints are the grand marketplace of welfare, O wise ones.
speaker: Dasganu
note: 'सन्नीतीची' read as 'सन्निधीची' (of the divine presence); 'विबुध हो' taken as addressing the listeners as 'O wise ones', though it could also mean 'O gods'.

meaning_en: Now my salutations, in every way, to all saints and holy men. Holding Dasganu's hand, may the writing of this book be done.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Taking Nivritti and Jnaneshwar, and Shri Tukaram of Dehu — these great ones who ferry across the ocean of worldly existence — salutations be to that Shri Ramdas.
speaker: Dasganu
check_note: The translation separates Shri Ramdas from the group described as 'great ones who ferry across the ocean of worldly existence' (हे भवाब्धीचें तारुं थोर). In the original, this phrase refers to all four saints (Nivritti, Jnaneshwar, Tukaram, and Ramdas) collectively. Also 'गहिनी' means 'including/along with' rather than 'Taking'. Corrected meaning: 'Including Nivritti, Jnaneshwar, and Shri Tukaram of Dehu — these great ones who ferry across the ocean of worldly existence — salutations be to that Shri Ramdas.'

meaning_en: O Samarth Sai of Shirdi, O virtuous Vaman Shastri, now give Dasganu assurance (fearlessness). May it be given as your own, O saints.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: By the grace of all of you, I will speak this. I, Dasganu, am your little one. Do not be harsh toward me.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: She who is a true mother is the one who teaches her child to speak. May the bond between you and me be like that of mother and child.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Therefore I will not now give all their names here; I simply point to the books Bhaktivijay and Bhaktamala.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: After that, I sang of each saint as they appeared, and composed three books. Look at them and you will understand that...
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Saint Shri Gajanan is a true match for those saints; the power of this incarnate person is certainly beyond the ordinary world.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: The saint biographies I sang earlier are good; I told them in summary form. Through those three books become wise.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Now I narrate this life-story in full - listen well. By my good fortune came the opportunity to compose this biography.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Nothing is impossible for you; everything is possible at your place. For Lankar's sake I make this effort, so that the book may be told easily.
speaker: Dasganu
note: "Lankar" is taken as a proper name (likely the person helping with the book, as in ovi 20), but the exact referent of the word is not certain.

meaning_en: The family deity of my family, the dweller of Kolhapur, the Mother of the world — I place my head at her feet, so that all may be auspicious.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: O Durga, Tulja Bhavani; O Aparna, Ambe, Mrudani — place your boon-bestowing hand on Dasganu's head.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Now, salutation to Dattatreya. Come quickly, mercifully, to my ink; to sing the Gajanan-charitra, give inspiration along with your grace.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Now, salutation to the lord sages beginning with Shandilya — Vasishtha, Gautama, Parashara — and to that Shankaracharya who is the sun in the sky of knowledge.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Saints have beaten such a drum of yours, O husband of Ramaa. That is why I have come to your door — now do not turn your face away from me.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: O Pandhariraya, give help to compose this saints' biography; sitting in my mind, this book will reach its pinnacle (kalasha).
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: O destroyer of worldly existence, O husband of Bhavani, O Nilkantha, O Gangadhara, O Omkara-formed Tryambakeshvara, place your boon-giving hand on my head.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: When your help is present, there is no fear even of Kala (Death); you turn iron into gold, like a philosopher's stone (paris).
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Your grace itself is the paris (philosopher's stone); I, Ganudas, am the iron. You help the destitute — do not trample me away again.
speaker: Dasganu
note: 'परतें मजला लोटूं नको' is ambiguous: 'परतें' can mean 'again' or 'in return', and 'लोटूं' literally means 'roll/trample'; read here as 'do not cast/trample me aside again'.

meaning_en: The good saint I first saw, near Akot, is the very one who remained at the end. Listen to the reason for this.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: In a rosary the small beads are strung first and the meru bead is joined afterwards; that is exactly the state reached in composing this biography.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: In Varhad there is a famous village named Shegaon, in the taluka named Khamgaon, where large trade is carried on.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: The village is small but of good conduct, yet its splendour is very great; because of the sadhu its name has become undying and imperishable in the three worlds.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: In that lake of Shegaon the lovely lotus Gajanan came into bloom, whose fragrance has pierced this entire universe.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Listen to that saint's life story calmly and attentively. To this day, saints have never caused harm or betrayal to anyone.
speaker: Dasganu
check_note: Adds 'attentively' not in original; 'सावकाश' means calmly/leisurely.

meaning_en: Saints are the guides of divine principles; saints are their ready cash, their living, tangible form. They are the unfailing carts of knowledge; loaded, they stand manifest in person.
speaker: Dasganu
note: The metaphors 'रोकडे' (ready cash) and 'गाडे भरले' (loaded carts) are compressed; this is a close figurative reading.
check_note: Adds interpretation 'their living, tangible form' for 'रोकडे' (ready cash).

meaning_en: One whose interest lies at the feet of saints — even Rukminikant is indebted to him. Now make the mind free of impurity, to listen to the life of Gajanan.
speaker: Dasganu
check_note: Adds 'even' not in original; 'ऐकावया' is 'let us listen' not infinitive 'to listen'.

meaning_en: In Bharatkhand, saints have come into being in great number. This festival has truly arrived, for the sake of the whole land.
speaker: Dasganu
check_note: Mistranslates 'अवांतर' (other/different) as 'whole'.

meaning_en: Jambudweep is blessed, blessed, from the very beginning. Of what happiness is this melody, which till today has never fallen here?
speaker: Dasganu
note: 'वाण' is read as वाणी (voice/melody); it could also mean 'arrow'. The sense is that such happiness has not descended here until now.

meaning_en: Princess Mirabai, whose devotion has no limit; for whose sake Sheshashayi drank poison.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Gorakh, Machchhendra and Jalander, who are lords of yoga; the Navanath Bhaktisar is the scripture of their divine play.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Those who, by pure devotion to Hari alone, won Shripati — they are Nama, the wise Narhari, and Jani and Kanho, friends of the saints.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Chokha, Savata and Kurmadas; Damajipant, a man of merit, for whose sake Vedaras, Hari, went and became a Mahar.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Mukundraj Janardan, who made the Niranjana fully known; whose life stories were sung later by Mahipati.
speaker: Dasganu
check_note: The Marathi 'मुकुंदराज जनार्दन' refers to two distinct saints (Mukundraj and Janardan), as confirmed by the plural 'ज्यांचीं' (whose). The meaning incorrectly treats them as a single person 'Mukundraj Janardan'. Corrected meaning: 'Mukundraj and Janardan, who made the Niranjan fully known; whose life stories were sung later by Mahipati.'

meaning_en: This Shegaon is a mine, and Gajanan is truly the diamond from it. Such is the influence of that Avliya (saint). I speak with limited understanding.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Now grasp this: hold love at Gajanan's feet. Your true uplift will come from this — do not forget it.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Gajanan's biography is a great cloud, and you listeners are all peacocks. When the water rains down in the form of this biography, you will surely dance.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: The townspeople of Shegaon are, for certain, of the highest good fortune; that is why they obtained Gajanan, this jewel of a saint.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Only when merit is to be earned does one obtain the feet of a saint. The best of saints are above even the gods; there is no doubt about this.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: This itself is the reason: that the feet of saints have been coming to and touching this land since time without beginning.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Narad, Dhruv, Kayadhu's son, Uddhav, Sudama, and Subhadra; the mighty son of Anjani; and Ajatashatru Dharmaraja.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Shankaracharya the Jagadguru, who were wish-fulfilling trees (kalpataru) for those who bowed at their feet and the Meru peak of the science of the Self — it was in this very land that they were born.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Madhva, Vallabha, Ramanuja — Adhokshaja himself is indebted to them; they who kept dharma's honor intact, displaying their own power.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Narsi Mehta, Tulsidas, Kabir, the wondrous Surdas — where would one ever finish describing the play (lila) of Lord Gaurang?
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: In the same way, something like this must have happened here by design. All of Gajanan's body bore the marks of yoga.
speaker: Dasganu
check_note: The translation adds 'by design' for 'निर्धारी' which means 'certainly/definitely', not 'by design'. Also 'something like this' is interpretive but acceptable given 'तैसेंच'. Corrected meaning: 'Similarly, something like this must have certainly happened here somewhere. All of Gajanan's body bore the marks of yoga.'

meaning_en: This will become clear to you later from their leelas. The profound glory of yoga is such that no one can fathom its depth.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: In Shegaon, in the month of Magh, on the day of Vadya Saptami, this rising of the ocean of knowledge took place, to ferry across those fallen into the pit.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: I now tell you the story of that time; listen. There was a devout householder whose name was Devidas.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: This Devidas, a virtuous man, was a descendant of the Paturkars, whose branch was Madhyandin; he was the head of a math.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Just as Brahma's whereabouts cannot be known by anyone, so certainty about him comes only from seeing Brahma himself.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Know a diamond that is radiant to be complete; seeing its brilliance, the knowers become absorbed in it.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Whose mine is that diamond from? On thinking about this, there is no need at all to bring it into consideration.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: In the very prime of youth, Gajanan came to the town of Shegaon, within Shaka 1818, on Magh vadya saptami (the seventh day of the dark fortnight of Magh).
speaker: Dasganu
check_note: Marathi text reads 'शके अठराशाभीतरीं' (within Shaka 1800), but meaning states 'within Shaka 1818'. Corrected meaning: 'In the very prime of youth, Gajanan came to the town of Shegaon, within Shaka 1800, on Magh vadya saptami (the seventh day of the dark fortnight of Magh).'

meaning_en: Some people say that from the place of Shri Samarth, from that Sajjangad, he came to this land.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Ramchandra Patil made a request to me: come to the kshetra of Pandhari for the Kartiki vari.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: In my mind there was a wish to sing the Gajanan-charitra, but its right occasion did not come together.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: To fulfill that desire of mine, the Samartha made this plan of Ramchandra.
speaker: Dasganu
note: "Samartha" (the capable one) is the one making the plan involving Ramchandra; the ovi does not name him.

meaning_en: The ways of a true saint cannot be understood by anyone. Mahapurusha Gajanan, a modern saint, a Chudamani among saints.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Where is this mahapurusha's place, or what trace is there of his caste? From the standpoint of history it is not found.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: The ritusanti ceremony of one of his children was taking place. For that occasion, preparations for a meal were underway at his house.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Leftover leaf-plates had been thrown on the road in front of the house of that brahmin Devidas.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: That Gajanan, the accomplished siddha-yogi, was sitting at that spot. On his body was a bandi (sleeveless jacket) made of old, worn-out cloth.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: He had no name or title of any kind with him, truly. For drinking water, he had a gourd (bhopla).
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: In his hand was an unbaked chillum of his own making, which had not yet been fired in a potter's kiln.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: His gaze was fixed on the tip of his nose, his posture calm; the power of austerity shone on his body. Like the first rays of dawn — how could one describe him?
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: His whole form was digambara (sky-clad); a feeling that eclipsed all sense of self and other; likes, dislikes and worldly conduct did not remain near him.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: That was the Samarth's swari (arrival); sitting on the road, he examined the leaf-plate (patravali), purely as his own divine play.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: When the food offering (shida) came before his eyes, he picked it up and put it into his mouth. The very purpose of doing this was to reveal that food is Parabrahman.
speaker: Dasganu
check_note: The Marathi text reads 'शीत' (cold/winter) but the context and translation require 'शिदा' (food offering). The translation 'food offering (shida)' corrects the likely typo in the source text rather than translating the word actually present.

meaning_en: For the shrutis (scriptures) proclaim aloud that food itself is Brahman, the hidden truth; the saying 'Annam brahmeti' (food is Brahman) stands in the Upanishads.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: To prove this, the cloud of mercy picks up the cold (food). But ordinary people did not understand its inner meaning.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Bankatlal Agarwala was walking along the road. He saw this scene, together with his dear friend.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Damodarpant Kulkarni — know that as the name of his friend. Both, on seeing that scene, were struck with astonishment.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: And they began saying to each other this truth: that his behaviour is contrary — he appears like a madman.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Though he is seeking food, he takes it only from a worthy person. Devidas also gives it to him, because he too is a virtuous man.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: He was radiant and captivating in appearance, with strong arms and neck, a stately chest and a steady gaze; his brow was knitted in a frown.
speaker: Dasganu
check_note: The phrase 'in a frown' is added; 'भृकुटी ठायीं झाली असे' means 'his brow was knitted/fixed' but does not specify a frown. Corrected meaning: He was radiant and captivating in appearance, with strong arms and neck, a stately chest and a steady gaze; his brow was knitted.

meaning_en: They saw the yogi absorbed in his own bliss and silently bowed to him, feeling contentment in their hearts.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: To Devidasbuva he said lovingly: "You, quickly fill a vessel with food and bring one outside."
speaker: the yogi
check_note: The phrase 'with food' is added; the Marathi only says 'fill a vessel' (पात्र वाढून). Corrected meaning: To Devidasbuva he said lovingly: 'You, quickly fill a vessel and bring one outside.'

meaning_en: Devidas did as told; he brought a vessel filled with cooked food and placed it at the doorway, before the Master.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: The all-capable Master sat to eat from the vessel that had been placed; no taste of anything remained within it — not even an atom was left.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: A wise person does not send away a beggar who comes to the door empty-handed. No logic works here; one must go by this one's deeds.
check_note: The meaning adds 'empty-handed' and 'one must go by' which are not present in the ovi. Corrected meaning: 'A wise person does not send back the beggar who came to the door. No logic works anywhere; by his deeds, this one.'

meaning_en: Bankatlal says to Pant, "Let us stand just like this on the road and keep watching this deed of his, in order to test it."
speaker: Bankatlal

meaning_en: True saints behave like madmen, outwardly, in the world — such is the saying of Vyasa spoken in the Bhagavat.
speaker: Bankatlal

meaning_en: By his deeds he appears mad, yet he seems laden with knowledge — or he may be a heap of pure knowledge, or perhaps that very thing in person.
speaker: Bankatlal
note: The last phrase 'asava kin prakatyaksha' is elliptical; best close reading is 'or might he be that (pure knowledge) itself in person.'

meaning_en: They began exchanging such thoughts with each other: when a jewel lies before you, only the gem-assayer truly knows it.
But there is no strong proof for it; still, there may be some meaning in what he says.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: All the people had become corrupt and were tormented by many afflictions; for their sake Samarth performed such a wonder.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: To bring about the uplift of the world, Samarth the siddhayogi again came upon earth, assuming incarnation in the form of Gajanan.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: A yogi can enter into any body; it is said the Jagadguru performed such a feat upon the earth.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Gorakh was born in a dung-heap, Kanifa in an elephant's ear, and Changdev in the Narayan pond; they appeared without a mother's womb.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Damodar began wiping; there was no water in the gourd. If He so willed, this servant was ready to give water.
speaker: Damodar
note: The object of 'wiping' is not stated in the ovi; from the context it appears to be the gourd.
check_note: The meaning mistranslates the second-person address in Damodar's speech. Marathi 'मर्जी असल्या' (if you wish) addresses Samarth directly, but the meaning uses third-person 'If He so willed'. Also 'तयार असे' (is ready) is present tense, rendered as past 'was ready'. Corrected meaning: "Damodar began wiping; there was no water in the gourd. 'If you wish, this servant is ready to give water.'"

meaning_en: Hearing these words, Samarth laughed. Looking at both of them, He said, "Listen, I tell you—"
speaker: Samarth

meaning_en: "Even if you have a need, then bring the water and pour it. The one Brahman is brimming full, pervading the whole universe."
speaker: Samarth

meaning_en: "In That, no difference of you and me remains, not even the slightest. Yet the world's conduct is true, and it must be observed."
speaker: Samarth

meaning_en: "Food is eaten by the body, therefore it needs water. This conduct the wise must surely understand."
speaker: Samarth

meaning_en: Therefore, for your cleverness, if you need a vessel, make arrangements for water; with that, everything is complete.
speaker: Shri Gajanan
check_note: The Marathi does not mention 'vessel'; it says 'गरज असल्या तुम्हां साची' (if you truly have need). The meaning adds 'vessel'. Corrected: 'Therefore, due to your cleverness, if you truly have need, make arrangement for water; that means everything is complete.'

meaning_en: Hearing this speech, both were overjoyed. Bankatlal said to Pant, 'Our fortune is blessed.'
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: To bring water, Damodar went into the house with the vessel. Listen to what happened there.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Beside the well there was a heap, a fixed spot where all the animals drank water.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Going there, they drank water and gave burps of satisfaction. Meanwhile, Pant brought the water back in the pot.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: May this Gajananvijay book bring delight to devotees. With joined hands, Dasganu begs this of Ishwar.
speaker: Dasganu
check_note: The Marathi 'आल्हादवो' is present indicative (delights/gives delight), not optative 'may bring delight'. 'विनवी' is a noun 'prayer', not verb 'begs'. The translation adds 'may' and converts noun to verb. Corrected: 'This Gajananvijay book delights devotees. With joined hands, Dasganu offers this prayer to Ishwar.'

meaning_en: In the same way, this elder in knowledge has gone mad for Subhadra in the form of liberation, the wretch. We should not take him now.
speaker: Bankatlal
note: 'याची आतां घेणें नको' is ambiguous: it can read as 'we should not take him (away/along) now' or 'we should no longer take him for a madman'; the first close reading is given.
check_note: The word 'कसवटी' (wretch) modifies the subject 'हा ज्ञानजेठी' (this elder in knowledge), but the translation places it after 'Subhadra', making it ambiguously refer to Subhadra. Corrected meaning: 'In the same way, this elder in knowledge, the wretch, has gone mad for Subhadra who is of the form of liberation. We should not accept him now.'

meaning_en: Blessed is our Shegaon — we have seen Yogirao with our own eyes. This fief-village 'Nirichha' (desirelessness) — Hari gave it to him.
speaker: Bankatlal
check_note: The Marathi says 'जयाला' (to Jaya / to victory), but the translation renders it as 'to him', changing the referent. Corrected meaning: 'Blessed is our Shegaon — we have seen Yogirao with our own eyes. This fief-village "Nirichha" (desirelessness) — Hari gave it to Jaya.'

meaning_en: The sun has reached midday; a patch of the ground has grown hot. The birds have gone and sat on a tree for shelter.
speaker: Bankatlal

meaning_en: In such blazing heat he sits in bliss. He is verily Brahman himself; no fear of anything has remained in him.
speaker: Bankatlal

meaning_en: He eats just as he pleases; there is no water in the tumba (gourd water-pot). O Pant, for that reason we should bring (water) and give (it to him).
speaker: Bankatlal

meaning_en: One who has been satisfied drinking the incomparable essence of Brahman — why would he ask for sweet buttermilk, sitting smacking his lips?
speaker: Dasganu
check_note: Mistranslation: 'गुळवण' means a sweet jaggery drink, not 'sweet buttermilk'. Corrected meaning: One who has been satisfied drinking the incomparable essence of Brahman — why would he ask for a sweet jaggery drink, sitting smacking his lips?

meaning_en: He who is the all-sovereign supreme king — to such a man, even if a jaghir is granted, love does not arise.
speaker: Dasganu
note: 'झाला असे साचार' is unclear; best close reading is 'of such true conduct'.

meaning_en: He made all the cooked dishes one; no liking or disliking remained; he satisfied his stomach's fire at the time of two prahars.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Seeing this, Bankatlal spoke to Pant: 'We called this one mad — that was without doubt a mistake.'
speaker: Bankatlal
check_note: Speaker is incorrect: the verse is narrated by Dasganu (the poet), not spoken by Bankatlal. The verse describes Bankatlal's action in third person. Corrected speaker: Dasganu.

meaning_en: For Subhadra at Dwaraka, Arjuna became mad in just this way; he forgot worldly conduct and began acting wildly.
speaker: Bankatlal

meaning_en: The drinker too is different, yet not different from it. God's unfathomable divine play is understood in this human birth.
speaker: Maharaj

meaning_en: Casting aside what was given, the mind is lost in worldly affairs. Contemplate always: from what has this world come into being?
speaker: Maharaj
note: 'तें दिलें' (what was given) is not specified in the ovi; its referent is unclear.

meaning_en: Hearing Samarth's words, both were overwhelmed. With single-minded devotion they became ready to roll at Samarth's feet.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Knowing their intent, Maharaj set off running. At that speed of the wind, who in the world can place an obstacle?
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: The story ahead will be narrated in the second chapter. Give attention, even a little, to listen to it.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Yes, yes, that muddy water — Samartha, do not put it to your mouth; that water, because of the animals — is it fit to drink?
note: 'योग्य आहे प्यावया' literally means 'it is fit to drink'; read here as a rhetorical question. The speaker is not named in the ovi or the context.

meaning_en: See, I have brought this water — sweet, clear and cold, scented in the proper way, with vala root put into it.
speaker: Damodarpant

meaning_en: Hearing this speech, Maharaj spoke in truth: 'These are all worldly tales — do not tell us such things.'
speaker: Maharaj
check_note: Missing 'worthless/insignificant' for 'avaghya'. Corrected meaning: 'Hearing this speech, Maharaj spoke in truth: These are all worldly worthless tales — do not tell us such things.'

meaning_en: All this is worthless stuff; Brahman pervades everything, in the proper way. There, muddy, clear and scented water — these distinctions do not remain.
speaker: Maharaj

meaning_en: The water is that very One; the clear and the muddy — He alone sees them. Good smell and bad smell, both of these, are His forms, without doubt.
speaker: Maharaj

meaning_en: Thousands of people went on the path, but no one saw them. Consider what is good from these two. Think about this!
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Diamonds and gravel were mixed together in one place. The appraiser selects the diamonds, throwing away the gravel.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: First, Bankatlal Agarwala came forward to question Gajanan. He came humbly.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Regarding the investigation of this letter-bundle, it is not understood why or where it is being done. Even if we are hungry, I will still arrange for food.
speaker: Bankatlal
note: The speaker is inferred from context as Bankatlal speaking to Gajanan; 'पत्रावळी' could mean a bundle of letters, a file, or a specific text.

meaning_en: He thought thus, but received no answer. He just looked up at the faces of both.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Thousands of people went on the path, but no one saw them. Consider what is good from these two. Think about this!
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Diamonds and pebbles mixed together in one place. The expert picks them out, discarding the pebbles and keeping the diamonds.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: First, Bankatlal Agarwala came forward. He came humbly to question Gajanan.
speaker: Dasganu

meaning_en: Regarding the examination of this document, somehow it is not understood. Even if we are hungry, I will still arrange for food.
speaker: Bankatlal
note: Speaker inferred from context as Bankatlal speaking about examining a letter/document; 'पत्रावळी' could mean letter, document or manuscript.

meaning_en: He thought thus. But no answer was found. He just looked up at both their faces.
speaker: Dasganu
